other_failure_modes.name: Feature scrambling due to incorrect extraction from sorted dataframe
other_failure_modes.description: When computing lag and rolling features for the validation and test sets, the combined dataframe is sorted by store and family, causing the new target rows to be interspersed. The code then incorrectly assumes the new rows are localized at the very end of the dataframe (`combined.iloc[start_idx:]`), leading to completely scrambled, mismatched features being assigned to the validation and test sets.

other_failure_modes.name: Overwriting historical target values with NaN
other_failure_modes.description: When preparing the combined dataframe for test feature engineering, the code explicitly sets the entire target column to NaN (`combined['sales'] = np.nan`), wiping out the historical training data. As a result, all lag and rolling features for the test set become NaN (and are subsequently filled with 0), destroying the predictive signal.

other_failure_modes.name: Train-serving skew / Target leakage in validation
other_failure_modes.description: For the validation set, lag and rolling features within the validation period are computed using the actual target values from that same period. However, during real multi-step test inference, these future actuals are unavailable, leading to a severe mismatch between validation and test features and overly optimistic validation scores.

summary: The solution employs a valid time-based split and extensive feature engineering with a LightGBM model. However, it contains multiple critical logic bugs in the feature engineering pipeline: it incorrectly extracts features from a sorted dataframe causing scrambled assignments, overwrites all historical test features with NaN, and introduces severe train-serving skew by using actual future target values to build validation features.
